subject: RFI: Implementation sequencing, cutover gating, and rollback criteria
messages:
From: Claire Evans <claire.evans@finova.com>
To: mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Procurement <procurement@finova.com>, Leo Wang <leo.wang@finova.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFI Follow-up: cutover sequencing and rollback criteria

Hi Mina,

Thanks for walking us through Redwood's capabilities last week. As we assemble responses for the internal RFI, procurement has asked us to provide a concrete implementation sequencing recommendation and explicit rollback criteria for our pilot -> production cutover. Specifically:

- A step-by-step sequence for onboarding (staging -> pilot -> canary -> general availability) with expected durations per step.
- Gating metrics for each stage (latency p95 targets, error budget thresholds, business KPIs).
- A short rollback decision tree and runbook references.

Can you share a draft that includes timings for a medium-complexity integration (SAML SSO, VPC peering, ingestion pipeline via Kafka, and embedding sync)? Procurement would like a version we can attach to the vendor evaluation packet by the end of May.

Also useful: a matrix of expected maintenance/change windows and any blackouts you require during cutover.

Best,
Claire
Claire Evans
Director, Vendor Evaluation | Finova
claire.evans@finova.com
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: RFI Follow-up: cutover sequencing and rollback criteria

Claire — thanks for the clear ask. Attached is a first-pass sequencing and a metrics template you can populate (redwood-cutover-metrics-template.xlsx). High-level sequencing for a medium-complexity integration (typical for customers of your size):

1) Preparation (1–2 weeks)
   - Account setup, SSO metadata exchange, VPC peering request, base network checks.
   - Deliverable: Integration checklist + test harness access.

2) Staging integration (2 weeks)
   - Model validation on representative data, secure credential exchange, end-to-end test of embedding sync and message flow.
   - Gating: p95 inference latency < 300ms (staging avg), embedding pipeline success rate > 99.5%.

3) Pilot (1–3 weeks)
   - Limited traffic (5–10%), parallel write-through logging to Finova systems, monitoring of business KPIs.
   - Gating: error rate < 0.5% vs baseline; user-facing KPI uplift (if applicable) non-negative.

4) Canary (1 week rolling across regions)
   - Gradual ramp to 25–30% across low-risk user segments. Focus on tail-latency and cache efficiency.
   - Gating: sustained p95 within SLA and no unhandled exceptions > 5/min.

5) GA cutover (1 day window with pre-approved fallbacks)
   - Final switch; short observation window (24–72 hours) with rollback triggers defined.

Rollback decision tree (summary):
- Severity 1 (service-facing errors impacting >1% of traffic or data loss): immediate rollback to previous model/endpoint; incident bridge & executive notify.
- Severity 2 (degraded performance, increased latency beyond SLO for >30 min): pause ramp, throttle traffic, enable fallback model variant.
- Severity 3 (minor spikes / intermittent errors): monitor for 2 business cycles; if recurring, pause and remediate.

I included the metrics template as an attachment and a short set of example gating thresholds. Marissa, Aditya — can you add proposed canary metrics and any automation we recommend for auto-rollback?

Thanks,
Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Mina / Claire — adding the canary gating specifics and automation hooks we usually propose. Forwarding the high-level checklist below.

--- Forwarded message ---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 15:20:00 -0700

Canary gating suggestions (automatable):
- Health checks: continuous synthetic probes hitting representative prompts every 30s per region (alert if 3 consecutive failures).
- Latency windows: 1-minute, 5-minute, and hourly p95 tracked; auto-throttle if p95 > threshold for 3 consecutive windows.
- Error budget consumption: track 24h burn rate vs baseline; auto-pause ramp if burn > 2x expected.
- Data drift: inline sampling of inputs vs training distribution; alert if KL divergence > threshold for three consecutive days.

Suggested automation actions:
- Auto-fallback to a smaller, quantized variant for latency spikes.
- Automated canary abort if combined health-check + error budget rules trip (decision threshold is configurable).

Runbook excerpts (short):
- Pre-cutover: confirm SLOs agreed, create canary cohort with user-ID hash seeds, schedule 2-hour dry-run in staging.
- During canary: maintain a realtime dashboard; Slack bridge to Finova on-call; 15-minute tactical cadence.
- Rollback: toggle routing policy to previous stable endpoint; mark the deployment as failed and collect forensic logs for 72h.

Mina — I attached a sample Prometheus/Alertmanager rule set in the runbook folder; we can export a trimmed version for the RFI deck.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal Customer Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Leo Wang <leo.wang@finova.com>

Subject: Re: RFI Follow-up: cutover sequencing and rollback criteria

Thanks for the draft — this is very helpful. A couple of constraints from our side to bake into the sequencing:

- Change freeze: corporate code freeze from 2027-06-20 to 2027-06-25 for fiscal month-end. Any planned GA cutover must avoid that window or have pre-approved exception.
- Maintenance window preference: weekends 02:00-06:00 PT.
- Audit/compliance: we need immutable audit logs for all routing changes and model updates (retention 1 year). Can you confirm Redwood can provide those logs and an export?

Also attaching our internal change-window matrix (finova-change-windows.pdf). If possible, align the pilot start so the GA cutover falls in early July. Procurement is particularly sensitive to documented rollback SLAs in the contract.

Best,
Leo
Leo Wang
Senior Engineer, Infrastructure | Finova
Attachment: finova-change-windows.pdf
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Claire Evans <claire.evans@finova.com>, Leo Wang <leo.wang@finova.com>

Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Finalized: Implementation sequencing and rollback criteria (RFI deliverable)

Claire / Leo — thanks for the constraints. We've adjusted the recommended timeline so GA cutover avoids Finova's freeze window and aligns with an early-July GA as requested. See attached RFI answer deck (rfi-answer-deck.pdf) and the metrics template we shared earlier. Key points (consolidated):

- Timeline (updated):
  • Preparation: 2027-06-07 -> 2027-06-13
  • Staging: 2027-06-14 -> 2027-06-27 (includes weekend dry-run 06/19)
  • Pilot: 2027-06-28 -> 2027-07-11 (5% -> 10% traffic)
  • Canary: 2027-07-12 -> 2027-07-18 (region-by-region ramp to 30%)
  • GA cutover: target 2027-07-22 (outside freeze window) with a 72h observation window
- Rollback & SLAs:
  • Immediate rollback for data-loss or >1% error impact (we will revert routing and reinstate previous stable endpoint within the 30-minute SLA).
  • Performance rollback: if p95 exceeds SLO for 45 continuous minutes during canary, we will pause ramp and either apply fallback variant or rollback fully depending on the triage.
  • Auditability: Redwood will provide immutable routing/model-change logs via a managed export (JSONL) with 1-year retention; details and sample export included in the deck.

- Operational hooks:
  • We will provide a shared Slack bridge and a temporary on-call rotation for the 72h GA observation window.
  • Prometheus/Alertmanager rules and a sample playbook excerpt are included.

Next steps: we will upload the final runbook and a trimmed Prometheus rule set to the Google Drive folder linked here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-cutover-runbook. Please confirm the date for a 60-minute run-through with Finova ops (propose 2027-06-18 09:00 PT).

I have attached the RFI answer slide deck for procurement. If Procurement wants, we can add a short contract exhibit listing rollback SLAs and audit export format.

Thanks — looking forward to the run-through.

Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
